metadata.description: The Columbus and Greenville main line Columbus - West Point - Mathiston - Eupora - Kilmichael - Winona - Carrollton - Greenwood - Itta Bena - Moorhead - Indianola - Stoneville - Greenville, Mississippi (167.6 mi), drawn by operator era: Richmond and Danville (leasing the Georgia Pacific) 1889-1894, Southern Railway (Southern Railway Company in Mississippi) 1894-1920, Columbus and Greenville 1920-1948; the 3 ft gauge Greenville, Columbus and Birmingham Greenville - Stoneville 1879-1881; and single-year [ANCHOR] features for the Southern's Tallahatchie Branch (Itta Bena - Webb, 1904) and Itta Bena - Belzoni (Delta Southern, 1909). Not via Starkville. Era features share identical geometry.

metadata.ownership_splits: Main line split at 1894 (Southern Railway in Mississippi took possession 1 Sep 1894) and 1920 (6 Nov 1920 rename to the Columbus & Greenville; Southern no longer ran the trains). Boundary years shared on both sides. The Aug 1923 receiver's sale (Columbus & Greenville Railroad -> Railway) is not a split: same display name and management. The January 1889 R&D lease precedes the June 1889 completion, so there is no Georgia Pacific-run era on the drawn main line. Delta Southern branch drawn as Southern Railway (the Southern operated it as agent).
omitted: [2] Columbus - Greenville football special 1957: American-Rails only, no date beyond the year; report says drawable NONE.
[5] Georgia Pacific pre-completion operation west of Columbus 1887-1889: no confirmable passenger year.
[6] Georgia Pacific narrow gauge Greenville - Johnsonville 1881-1889: no dated passenger evidence.
[8] GC&B Stoneville - Johnsonville 1881: unknown whether it opened before the Oct 1881 GP purchase.
[10] Columbus and Greenville Tallahatchie Branch after 1920: no passenger evidence.
[12] Itta Bena and Belzoni Railroad 1923-1928: no passenger evidence (described as a freight operation).
[13] Southern Deer Creek Branch Stoneville - Richey and [14] Elizabeth - Kergs Junction: Fowler lists passenger stops but no year.
All freight-only years: C&G main line after 1948 (Feb 1952 Official Guide daggers every station freight-only), Illinois Central Gulf 1972-1975, CAGY 1975-present (Rule 1).
metadata.freight_only: No freight-only segment drawn; segments end at the last passenger year. Post-1948 freight, ICG and CAGY operation is mentioned in notes only.
not_yet_sourced: Main line passenger end: 1948 (Hawkins; American-Rails last Deltan 15 Jul 1948) vs 1949 (American-Rails 'all scheduled passenger service ended in 1949'); latest primary confirmation 1947 (Fowler d). A Greenville or Columbus newspaper 'last train' story would settle it.
GC&B start: American-Rails gives both April 1878 service and a January 1879 first spike; drawn from 1879, low confidence.
R&D lease of the Georgia Pacific dated January 1889 by railga.com only; Poor's Manual 1890-1894 would confirm. If wrong, 1889-1894 should be Georgia Pacific in part or whole.
[ANCHOR] Tallahatchie Branch 1904 and Itta Bena - Belzoni 1909: one dated year each; actual opening and passenger-end years unknown.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates.

segments.note: The independent Columbus and Greenville. Start 1920: on 6 Nov 1920 the Southern Railway Company in Mississippi's charter was amended, renaming it the Columbus & Greenville Railroad, and it was placed in receivership (A. T. Stovall receiver, June 1921) - from then the Southern no longer ran these trains (msrailroads C&G.htm; Hawkins timeline). Sold at receiver's sale 6 Aug 1923 to Stovall and local interests and renamed Columbus & Greenville Railway - same display name and same man in charge, so not split here. Service: the Deltan (C&G 11/12) with an across-platform connection at Columbus to Southern 11/12 for Atlanta, air-conditioned 1938; Brill gas-mechanical car M-75 (1925) on Winona - Greenville locals to c.1930; Brill gas-electric sets M-76/M-77 from late 1928 to 1948; a daily mixed train (Hawkins motorcars/passenger pages, citing Beebe & Clegg 1961). Primary-source touch-downs: Fowler's line 67 letters b (1928 company timetable) and d (1947 Official Guide) on stations end to end. END 1948 is the earlier side of a 1948-1949 bracket and rests on secondary sources: American-Rails gives the last run of the Deltan as 15 Jul 1948 and says 'all scheduled passenger service ended in 1949'; Hawkins says the Deltan was eliminated in 1947 and the mixed carried passengers until the Post Office moved the mail to trucks in 1948 ('cessation of all C&G passenger service in 1948'). The latest PRIMARY confirmation is 1947 (Fowler d). The Feb 1952 Official Guide index marks every C&G station freight-only - consistent, but not itself an end date. Freight continued; Illinois Central Gulf 1972, the new CAGY from 1975, West Point - Greenwood embargoed 2001. A 1957 Columbus - Greenville football special (American-Rails only) is not drawn. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE (one Deltan or motor-car round trip plus a daily mixed each way in the 1940s, from Hawkins' prose, not a timetable).
sources: Segment-level: start from the 6 Nov 1920 charter amendment (msrailroads C&G.htm, Hawkins timeline); 1928 and 1947 touch-downs from Fowler SL246 line 67 legend b/d; end 1948 from American-Rails (last Deltan 15 Jul 1948) and Hawkins (mixed ended 1948) - secondary, end bracket 1948-1949. Headway estimated. Per research/branches/columbus_and_greenville_railway.txt block [1].

segments.note: Southern Railway Company in Mississippi, a Mississippi-chartered subsidiary of the Southern Railway (required by state law; stock held through the Southern-controlled National Investment Co., ICC valuation draft). Formed 30 Aug 1894 and took possession of the Georgia Pacific's Mississippi property at the foreclosure 1 Sep 1894 (msrailroads SRM.htm; ICC valuation draft; American-Rails). Part of the Southern's Atlanta - Birmingham - Columbus - Greenville route, with a through Pullman for many years (American-Rails). Primary touch-down: Fowler line 67 letter a, the 1913 Southern public timetable, on e.g. Elliott and Brownings. On 1 Jan 1909 the company took over most of the Southern's other Mississippi property (ICC draft) - a corporate reshuffle, not a change of who ran these trains. Ends 6 Nov 1920 when the charter was amended to make it the Columbus & Greenville (an operator end, not a service end - continues as the Columbus and Greenville feature). Headway 1440 min is an ESTIMATE (at least one through train each way daily is implied by the through-Pullman route; no timetable frequency was read).
sources: Segment-level: start 30 Aug / 1 Sep 1894 from msrailroads SRM.htm, the ICC valuation draft and American-Rails; 1913 touch-down from Fowler SL246 line 67 legend a; end at the 6 Nov 1920 rename (msrailroads C&G.htm). Headway estimated. Per research/branches/columbus_and_greenville_railway.txt block [3].

segments.note: The Georgia Pacific Railway's Columbus - Greenville line, operated by the Richmond & Danville under a lease dated January 1889 (railga.com - a SINGLE secondary source; if disproved, some or all of this era should be relabelled Georgia Pacific). Fowler's heading for the Southern in Mississippi reads 'ex Georgia Pacific; Richmond & Danville', consistent with R&D operation. Columbus - Greenville completed 18 Jun 1889 (msrailroads, Hawkins, American-Rails); through scheduled service began 8 Jul 1889 (American-Rails). Ends at the 30 Aug / 1 Sep 1894 transfer to the Southern Railway Company in Mississippi (operator end - continues as the Southern Railway feature). Any Georgia Pacific operation of pieces west of Columbus before June 1889, and the narrow-gauge Greenville - Johnsonville end 1881-1889, have no dated passenger evidence and are not drawn. Headway 1440 min is an ESTIMATE (through Atlanta - Greenville route; no timetable frequency read).
sources: Segment-level: start from the 18 Jun 1889 completion and 8 Jul 1889 first through service (American-Rails; msrailroads GeorgiaPacific.htm; Hawkins timeline); R&D operation from the January 1889 lease (railga.com, single source); end at the 1894 Southern takeover (msrailroads SRM.htm). Headway estimated. Per research/branches/columbus_and_greenville_railway.txt block [4].

segments.note: The 3 ft gauge Greenville, Columbus & Birmingham Railroad (chartered 1872), steam, Greenville - Fish Lake - Buckner - Stoneville. START CONFLICT: American-Rails says track reached Stoneville 31 Mar 1878 and 'first scheduled passenger service began April 8, 1878, with two daily round trips between Greenville and Stoneville', but the same page gives the first spike at Greenville as 5 Jan 1879, which cannot both be true; Hawkins says the first tracks were laid in 1878. Drawn from the later year, 1879 - low confidence, and 1879 is itself not proven if the January 1879 spike date is right. Extended through Indianola to Johnsonville in 1881 (Hawkins) - whether before or after the October 1881 sale is unknown, so the extension is not drawn. Ends October 1881 when the Georgia Pacific bought the road (operator end); the Georgia Pacific's 1881-1889 operation has no dated passenger evidence and is not drawn. Headway 720 min is taken from American-Rails' 'two daily round trips', a secondary and internally inconsistent source - treat as an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: start from American-Rails (Apr 1878 service vs Jan 1879 first spike - conflict, later year used) and Hawkins timeline (tracks 1878); end at the October 1881 Georgia Pacific purchase (msrailroads GeorgiaPacific.htm, Hawkins). Per research/branches/columbus_and_greenville_railway.txt block [7]. Low confidence.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] The Southern's Tallahatchie Branch, Itta Bena - Schlater - Minter City - Glendora - Webb. Fowler lists its stations as passenger stops; the only dated mark is 'Sturdivants 1904t' (the 1904 Southern public timetable), so 1904 is the single proven passenger year. Service certainly ran wider both ways but no other year is confirmed: one web-search summary dates the line's construction to 1891 (anachronistically to 'Southern Railway', which did not exist until 1894), and when passengers ended is unknown - the branch passed to the Columbus & Greenville in 1920 and no C&G-era passenger evidence was found (not drawn). Do not widen this anchor without a dated source. Headway 1440 min is an ESTIMATE (a mixed or local each way daily is assumed; no frequency read).
sources: Segment-level: 1904 anchor from Fowler SL246 SOU 2 'Sturdivants 1904t'. Start and end NOT SOURCED. Per research/branches/columbus_and_greenville_railway.txt block [9].

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Itta Bena - Morgan City - Swiftown - Jaketown - Belzoni, built October 1906 by the Delta Southern Railway (msrailroads DeltaSou.htm), a Southern subsidiary that never ran its own trains: operated by the Southern from 26 Mar 1906 and by the Southern Railway in Mississippi as agent from 11 Feb 1909 (ICC valuation draft), hence drawn as Southern Railway. The only dated passenger evidence is Fowler's former station names 'Morgan 1909G' and 'Swift 1909G' - the stations appear in the 1909 Official Guide, a passenger publication (a station-name entry, weaker than a timetable with times). 1909 is the single proven year; service certainly ran wider both ways but no other year is confirmed. The C&G got ICC permission to abandon it in 1921 (Hawkins western; MDAH finding aid); the Itta Bena & Belzoni Railroad ran it 1923-1928 with no passenger evidence (not drawn); abandoned 1928 - an abandonment year, not a passenger end. Do not widen this anchor without a dated source. Headway 1440 min is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: 1909 anchor from Fowler SL246 SOU 3 'Morgan 1909G', 'Swift 1909G'; construction and operator from msrailroads DeltaSou.htm and the ICC valuation draft. Start and end NOT SOURCED. Per research/branches/columbus_and_greenville_railway.txt block [11].
